input.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that cuts to R&D spending were the MAIN reason Intel's operating loss narrowed in 2025.

From the full-year 2025 data (E16), Intel's operating loss improved from -$11,678 million in 2024 to -$2,214 million in 2025, an improvement of $9,464 million.

From E13, R&D expenses decreased by $2.8 billion (17%) in 2025 compared to 2024. This is a significant reduction but represents only about 30% of the total operating loss improvement.

From E17, restructuring and other charges decreased from $11,679 million in 2024 to $2,221 million in 2025, a reduction of $9,458 million. This reduction alone accounts for virtually the entire operating loss improvement.

From E15, the Corporate Unallocated expenses (which include restructuring charges per E11 and E12) improved from -$11,177 million in 2024 to -$5,518 million in 2025, an improvement of $5,659 million.

The evidence clearly shows that the reduction in restructuring and other charges ($9.5 billion) was far larger than the R&D savings ($2.8 billion). The restructuring charge reduction was more than three times the size of R&D cuts and alone accounts for nearly 100% of the operating loss improvement. Therefore, R&D cuts were NOT the main reason for the narrowing - the reduction in restructuring charges was.

None of the challenges successfully weakened this conclusion. H1 found no management attribution to R&D as the primary driver. H2 confirmed that restructuring charges are reported separately but are still part of operating income. H3 confirmed the full-year data shows the same pattern as the nine-month data.
